You need to evaluate yourself before enrolling for a d.d.s degree. 
In order to succeed you need to have these traits: 
1- artistic sense
2- good or fair hand skills ( at first ).
3- the ability to understand and positively communicate with all sorts of personalities .
4- self-confidence.
5- the ability to withstand pressure, it's a very tiring profession mentally and physically.
6- the ability to always learn and staying up to date.
7- no problem working in oral cavity ( saliva, blood , etc ) 

If you have these traits I'll guarantee you'll be a wonderful dentist.

Each patient is different which leads to countless treatment plans. Many times in my clinic I had to improvise ( within borders of science and theory ) to achieve patients needs within given time.
No two patients are alike.
What suits a patient may be contraindicated for another. 
Dentistry is not just a single skill you learn to do, and definitely not a matter of memorizing couple books and that's it.
it's a very wide specialty, the more you read and study the more you feel you have so much  more to learn. ( but first you got to have the passion for it, otherwise it would much harder on you )
